newsitem.title: GERMANY: AMB 96 net profit rises about 30 pct.
newsitem.headline: AMB 96 net profit rises about 30 pct.

text.p: (in millions of marks unless otherwise stated)
Dividend (including tax credit) 22.85 dmk vs n/a
NOTE - Full name of the German insurer is the AMB Holding group, which mainly comprises the Aachener und Muenchener Beteiligungs-AG parent company.
The company also said that it expected its earnings per share for 1996 to rise sharply.

The reason for the sharp rise in parent pre-tax profit was a higher return from shareholdings, AMB said. However tax charges rose sharply, by 24.8 million marks to 61.4 million marks, making the net profit rise less dramatic.
The insurer said it allocated 55 million marks to its parent company reserves.

Insurance business accounted for some 17 billion marks of the total group sales. Insurance premiums rose around 4.9 percent, with domestic premiums rising 4.4 percent and foreign premiums up 9.7 percent, with Dutch business showing especially strong growth.
Life insurance business accounted for 9.3 billion marks of premium income, up from 8.8 billion the previous year.
Group capital investments rose seven percent to more than 73 billion marks.
